Encoding.Description:

Allowed patterns: SOP2 (32 bits) SOP2 + LITERAL (64 bits)

Scalar memory operations.
Examples:
// Load some resource constants into SGPRs s_load_dwordx4 s[20:23], s[0:1], 0x0 // pos resource buffer s_load_dwordx4 s[24:27], s[0:1], 0x4 // color0 resource buffer s_load_dwordx4 s[28:31], s[0:1], 0x10 // tex0 resource buffer
Different ways of writing an offset:
s_load_dword s20, s[0:1], null // No offset applied s_load_dword s20, s[0:1], s4 // Register-based offset only s_load_dword s20, s[0:1], s4 offset:0x8 // Apply register and constant offsets
To simplify porting older shader programs, instructions accepting a constant offset may either specify the offset as an operand (to match old architectures that did not allow for an SGPR offset) or they may use the offset: modifier. If a constant operand is used then the offset: modifier may not be used, and the instruction is translated to the current binary format as shown below:
s_load_dword s20, s[0:1], 0x8 // Constant offset only, in operand s_load_dword s20, s[0:1], null offset:0x8 // Identical to above, using modifier, matches hardware
The second example reflects the current binary encoding of the instruction.

Encoding.Description:
Vector ALU operations with one destination and one source. Instructions in this encoding may be promoted to VOP3 unless otherwise noted. Instructions in this encoding may use SDWA or DPP modes unless otherwise noted.
Allowed patterns: VOP1 (32 bits) VOP1 + LITERAL (64 bits) VOP1 + SDWA (64 bits) VOP1 + DPP (64 bits)

Vector ALU comparison operations with two sources. Instructions in this encoding may be promoted to VOP3 unless otherwise noted. Note that vector compare instructions respect the EXEC mask for computing the result in each thread; if EXEC[laneId] is zero, then the comparison for that thread is not performed and the result of VCC[laneId] is zero. SDWA is allowed but DPP is not allowed.
Note when using SDWA format, the SDWA_SDST_ENC format must be used; this means the dst_sel, dst_unused, omod and clamp modifiers are unavailable.
Allowed patterns: VOPC (32 bits) VOPC + LITERAL (64 bits) VOPC + SDWA (64 bits)

Encoding.Description:
Flat (DUA) global addressing instructions.
For global instructions note that a VGPR address must be specified. In sp3 an SGPR address may be omitted by specifying "off" or "null" in the SADDR operand slot ("off" is a legacy syntax and is translated to "null").

Field.Description: Something about GL2 cache control; also known as the Fowler bit.
If set, operation is globally coherent.
Write Data to LDS. Must be zero for all stores and atomics.

Encoding.Description:
Flat (DUA) scratch addressing instructions.
For scratch instructions at most one of a VGPR address or an SGPR address must be specified. Both addresses cannot be used.
For no address, in sp3 specify "off" or "null" for both the ADDR and SADDR operand slots. In binary microcode the SADDR field is set to 0x7f (EXEC_HI), this is not a real operand but instead signals a case of no address.
For only a vector address, in sp3 specify "off" or "null" for the SADDR operand slot. This generates "null" in the SADDR field ("off" is a legacy syntax).
For only a scalar address, in sp3 specify "off" or "null" for the ADDR operand slot. This causes SADDR to be generated normally, which in turn causes hardware to ignore the ADDR operand.

Field.Description: Something about GL2 cache control; also known as the Fowler bit.
If set, operation is globally coherent.
Write Data to LDS. Must be zero for all stores and atomics.

FunctionalGroup.Name: SALU
FunctionalGroup.Description: Scalar ALU (SALU) instructions operate on values that are common to all work-items in the wave. These operations consist of 32-bit integer or floating-point arithmetic, and 32 or 64-bit bitwise operations, and they store results in scalar registers.

FunctionalGroup.Name: SMEM
FunctionalGroup.Description: Scalar Memory (SMEM) instructions allow a shader program to load data from memory into scalar registers, making the data accessible to all work-items in the wave.

FunctionalGroup.Name: VALU
FunctionalGroup.Description: Vector ALU (VALU) instructions perform arithmetic or logical operations on data for each of the wave's work-item and write results back to vector registers, scalar registers or the EXEC mask.

FunctionalGroup.Name: VMEM
FunctionalGroup.Description: Vector-memory (VMEM) instructions transfer data to and from vector registers, making the data uniquely available for each work-item in the wave.

FunctionalGroup.Name: EXPORT
FunctionalGroup.Description: Export instructions copy data from a VGPR to one of the export buffers (position, color, or Z).

FunctionalGroup.Name: BRANCH
FunctionalGroup.Description: Branch instructions allow programs to jump - direct or indirect - to an instruction to be executed next, conditionally or unconditionally.

FunctionalGroup.Name: MESSAGE
FunctionalGroup.Description: Message instructions send a message to fixed function hardware or the host and can be used to request that a value be returned to the wave.

FunctionalGroup.Name: WAVE_CONTROL
FunctionalGroup.Description: Wave control instructions control a wave's execution these include dependency, delay, scheduling, and wave termination operations.

FunctionalGroup.Name: TRAP
FunctionalGroup.Description: Trap instructions transition into and out of the wave's trap handler
